title: Unstraightening equivalence on the homotopy theory of right fibrations
statement:
Use simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], right fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and $D=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$, the projective category $\mathcal P_S$, the ordered-cone functor $L_S$ and its right adjoint $U_S$ defined in [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction]. Fix any small simplicial set $S$ in a universe enlarged when necessary. Let $\mathcal P_S^{cf}$ be the full simplicial subcategory on projectively cofibrant and projectively fibrant presheaves. Let $\operatorname{RFib}(S)$ have as objects all right fibrations $E\to S$ and mapping simplicial sets $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(E,E')_n=\{E\times\Delta^n\to E'\text{ over }S\}$, with composition by evaluation and the diagonal of $\Delta^n$.

The unstraightening $U_S$ induces a Dwyer--Kan equivalence $\mathcal P_S^{cf}\to\operatorname{RFib}(S)$. Explicitly, $U_S(F)\to S$ is a right fibration for every projectively bifibrant $F$, the induced maps $\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(F,G)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(U_S(F),U_S(G))$ are weak homotopy equivalences, and every right fibration $E\to S$ is simplicially homotopy equivalent over $S$ to $U_S(F)$ for some projectively bifibrant $F$. In the last assertion this means that there exist maps $e:E\to U_S(F)$ and $r:U_S(F)\to E$ over $S$ such that $re$ and $1_E$, and $er$ and $1_{U_S(F)}$, are connected by maps from the respective products with $\Delta^1$ over $S$. The enrichment on $U_S$ is the canonical one induced on simplexwise cone mapping spaces by the natural cosimplicial map $Q^n\to\Delta^n$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. No assertion about fibrant objects or weak equivalences of a slice model structure is assumed, and $S$ need not be a quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.11, with the simplex comparison of Lemmas 2.2.3.7, 2.2.3.9 and 2.2.3.10 and the descent proof on pp. 83-85. Only the adjunction/preservation part of Theorem 2.2.1.2 and a separately constructed mono/cone model are used in that proof; neither Corollary 2.2.3.12 nor Corollary 2.2.3.13 is an input. No Stacks tag states this result. HTT reading copy is in the sandbox; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For a projectively fibrant $F$ and a right-horn lifting problem over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$, adjunction converts the problem into extending a map $L_S(\Lambda_i^n)\to F$ across $L_S(\Delta^n)$. The cone-adjunction statement makes this inclusion a projective cofibration, and the right-horn comparison [lem-coef-unstraightening-simplex-pointwise] makes it an objectwise weak equivalence. Since $F\to *$ is a projective fibration, its defining lifting property supplies the extension. Thus $U_S(F)\to S$ is a right fibration. The same comparison identifies its fiber at $s$ with $\operatorname{Sing}_Q F(s)$, naturally weakly equivalent to $F(s)$. Consequently an objectwise weak equivalence between fibrant diagrams induces a vertex-fiber weak equivalence of right fibrations; [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent-gluing] makes this an over-base simplicial homotopy equivalence. These arguments require neither cofibrancy of $F$ nor a slice model structure.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2 (preservation only), Remark 2.2.2.11 and Lemma 2.2.3.6; read online, archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag for this result.

proof.text: Here is the enrichment construction, without assuming an enriched adjunction. For an enriched diagram $H$ on $D$, adjoin one last object $v$ to $D^{\mathrm{op}}$, with mixed mapping objects $H(d)$, outgoing mapping objects empty and endomorphism object at $v$ equal to $\Delta^0$; mixed composition is the action of $H$. By the cone pushout universal property, an $m$-simplex of $U_SH$ above $\sigma$ is precisely a simplicial functor from $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m\star\Delta^0]$ to this category, prescribed on the initial face and on the last object. For $H=F\times K$, this functor consists of the cone functor for $F$ and a cone functor constant on the initial face with mixed target $K$. The latter factors through the collapsed cone $J^m$ and is exactly a map $Q^m\to K$. Pairing and projection are inverse, giving $U_S(F\times K)\cong U_SF\times\operatorname{Sing}_QK$. All simplex operators restrict cone functors, so these identifications commute with them, with diagram maps, and with iterated products. Precomposition with $Q^m\to\Delta^m$ gives $K\to\operatorname{Sing}_QK$, preserving products and the terminal object degreewise. Applying $U$ to an enriched map $F\times K\to G$ and precomposing therefore gives $U_SF\times K\to U_SG$. Naturality in $K$ defines the required map of mapping simplicial sets. Units are preserved because the terminal factor has its unique cone functor; composition is preserved because both composites send a pair of parameter maps to their pair, followed by the diagonal. This is exactly the enrichment specified in the item.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.12; explicit cone-functor construction; read online, archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag for this result.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal D(S)=\mathcal P_S^f[W_S^{-1}]$ and $\mathcal R(S)=\operatorname{RFib}(S)[V_S^{-1}]$, using the enriched simplicial localizations of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]; $V_S$ consists of vertex-fiber weak equivalences. The right-fibration mapping lemma makes $\operatorname{RFib}(S)$ locally Kan and makes every member of $V_S$ an equivalence in its path-component category. Thus the canonical functor $\operatorname{RFib}(S)\to\mathcal R(S)$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. The same localization-calculus statement makes $\mathcal P_S^{cf}\to\mathcal D(S)$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. The enriched functor of Step 2 preserves the specified arrows by Step 1 and therefore induces an enriched comparison $\phi_S:\mathcal D(S)\to\mathcal R(S)$, with its commutative square from $\mathcal P_S^{cf}\to\operatorname{RFib}(S)$. Apply [lem-coef-unstraightening-strict-base-change] in its presheaf presentation: diagram restriction, right-fibration pullback and the enriched comparisons commute strictly with every base map. Its preservation clauses give well-defined restriction functors on the localized fibrant categories; functoriality of the cited localization construction therefore supplies the strict restriction cones used in Steps 4--6. Let $\mathscr V$ be the class of bases for which $\phi_S$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. The standard-simplex theorem [lem-coef-unstraightening-simplex-dk-equivalence] and the two vertical Dwyer--Kan equivalences put every $\Delta^n$ in $\mathscr V$. This uses enriched localizations throughout, with no coherent-nerve equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.11, initial localization diagram, and Lemma 2.2.3.10; read online, archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag for this result.

proof.text: The class $\mathscr V$ is invariant under isomorphisms and closed under arbitrary small coproducts, including the empty coproduct. Indeed [lem-coef-projective-diagram-simplicial-descent] makes $\mathcal D(\coprod S_j)$ the homotopy product of the $\mathcal D(S_j)$. A simplicial set over a disjoint union is uniquely its disjoint union of pullbacks, degreewise, and a right-horn lifting problem lies in one summand. Maps and their simplicial parameter families decompose into families on the summands. Thus $\operatorname{RFib}(\coprod S_j)=\prod_j\operatorname{RFib}(S_j)$ with its actual mapping spaces; over the empty base there is one object with terminal mapping set. These right-fibration categories are fibrant simplicial categories: their mapping complexes are Kan by Step 3 and the model convention in [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus] identifies this with fibrancy. A discrete diagram of fibrant objects is fibrant in the diagram model, so its ordinary product computes its derived limit. Hence this actual product is also a homotopy product. The canonical Dwyer--Kan equivalences $\operatorname{RFib}(T)\to\mathcal R(T)$ from Step 3 identify its cone with a homotopy-product cone for the $\mathcal R(S_j)$. Base-change naturality identifies $\phi_{\coprod S_j}$ with the comparison of the two homotopy-product cones. If every $\phi_{S_j}$ is an equivalence then this comparison is an equivalence: replace the discrete diagrams by fibrant diagrams, compute their derived products by ordinary products, and use that products of weak equivalences of Kan mapping complexes and equivalences of path-component categories are equivalences. This uses products of Kan complexes, not unrestricted products of nonfibrant simplicial sets.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.11, conditions (i) and (ii); read online, archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag for this result.

proof.text:
Suppose $P=B\amalg_A C$, with $A\hookrightarrow B$ a monomorphism and $A,B,C\in\mathscr V$. The enriched diagram-descent theorem [lem-coef-projective-diagram-simplicial-descent] identifies $\mathcal D(P)$ with the homotopy limit of the three diagram categories. Replacing these by $\mathcal R(A),\mathcal R(B),\mathcal R(C)$ via $\phi$ shows that the composite
$$\mathcal D(P)\xrightarrow{\phi_P}\mathcal R(P)\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal R(B)\times^h_{\mathcal R(A)}\mathcal R(C)$$
is an equivalence. Apply the comparison criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus] with $\beta=\phi_P$. It remains to check the mapping-space square for every pair $E,E'$ of right fibrations over $P$. Apply [lem-coef-right-fibration-pushout-mapping-square] with $X=E$ and $Y=E'$. Its hypotheses hold: the base square is the stated simplicial pushout, $A\to B$ is mono, and $E'\to P$ is a right fibration. It gives the strict pullback square of actual mapping complexes, its Kan-fibration leg, and its comparison with the path homotopy pullback. The canonical Dwyer--Kan equivalences from right-fibration categories to their enriched localizations identify their actual mapping complexes with those in the required square. Every object of a localization is represented up to equivalence by an object of the original category, so this checks all pairs. Thus $\alpha$ is an equivalence; since $\alpha\phi_P$ is an equivalence, $\phi_P$ is one too. This proves pushout closure, including essential surjectivity, without asserting that right-fibration objects glue strictly.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.11, pushout comparison diagram and mapping-square argument on printed pp.84-85; read online, archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag for this result.

proof.text: For an increasing sequence $S_0\subseteq S_1\subseteq\cdots$ in $\mathscr V$ with union $S$, the diagram-descent theorem gives $\mathcal D(S)\simeq\operatorname{holim}_n\mathcal D(S_n)$. The comparison criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus], applied to $\alpha:\mathcal R(S)\to\lim_n\mathcal R(S_n)$ and $\beta=\phi_S$, reduces the assertion $S\in\mathscr V$ to mapping spaces. For fixed $E,E'$ over $S$, the mapping complex over $S$ is the strict inverse limit of the mapping complexes over $S_n$: a compatible family of maps on the increasing union $E=\bigcup_n E|_{S_n}$ gives a unique map, also with every parameter $\Delta^m$. The transition maps are Kan fibrations by [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent-gluing]. The strict inverse limit therefore computes the homotopy limit of spaces, by the Kan-tower assertion of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. The canonical Dwyer--Kan equivalences from right-fibration categories to their enriched localizations identify the actual complexes with those used by the criterion. All localization objects are represented up to equivalence by right fibrations. Hence $\alpha$, and then $\phi_S$, are equivalences.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.11, condition (v), with the omitted increasing-union argument supplied; read online, archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag for this result.

proof.text: We now prove every small base is in $\mathscr V$, explicitly carrying out the generation argument. The empty base is in $\mathscr V$ by Step 4. Induct on $n$ to prove that every simplicial set of dimension at most $n$ lies in $\mathscr V$. For such a set $T$, its $(n-1)$-skeleton and every copy of $\partial\Delta^n$ have dimension at most $n-1$; for $n=0$ they are empty. The boundary-cell decomposition [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], applied to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow T$, presents $T$ as the pushout of its $(n-1)$-skeleton and the coproduct of its nondegenerate $n$-simplices along the coproduct of their boundaries. The induction hypothesis, coproduct closure and the simplex case put the three corners in $\mathscr V$. The boundary inclusion is a monomorphism, so Step 5 puts $T$ in $\mathscr V$. Finally an arbitrary $S$ is the increasing union of its finite-dimensional skeleta, each already in $\mathscr V$; Step 6 puts $S$ in $\mathscr V$. All the indexing sets and the countable sequence are small in the enlarged universe.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.5, proof by skeleta, used in Proposition 2.2.3.11; read online, archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag for this result.

proof.text: Thus $\phi_S$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence for the given arbitrary small $S$. In the commutative square of Step 3, both vertical functors are Dwyer--Kan equivalences by [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. Two-out-of-three for weak homotopy equivalences on mapping sets, and for equivalences of path-component categories, therefore shows that the actual enriched $U_S:\mathcal P_S^{cf}\to\operatorname{RFib}(S)$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. In particular its maps $\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(F,G)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(U_SF,U_SG)$ are weak homotopy equivalences. Choose a bifibrant $F$ and an isomorphism from any given $E$ to $U_SF$ in the path-component category. That isomorphism and its inverse are represented by vertices $e,r$ of the corresponding mapping complexes. The composites lie in the identity components. The mapping complexes are Kan by [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent-gluing]; filling horns reverses edges and concatenates successive edges, so each finite path can be represented by one edge with the desired endpoints. These two edges are maps from $E\times\Delta^1$ and $U_SF\times\Delta^1$ over $S$, with endpoints $(re,1_E)$ and $(er,1_{U_SF})$. With right-fibration valuedness from Step 1 these are every asserted clause, for the specified enrichment and without a slice model structure. The Dwyer--Kan definition in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] applies directly.

lean.statement: theorem unstraightening_homotopy_descent (S : SSet.{u}) : ∃ (C : ConeSimplexCoordinates S) (π : PinchedCube.qFunctor.{u} ⟶ stdSimplex.{u}), (∀ k : ℕ, PinchedCube.quotientMap k ≫ π.app ⦋k⦌ = PinchedCube.maximumMap k) ∧ ∃ U : CanonicalEnrichment C π, (∀ F : Bifibrant S, Enhanced.rightFibration (rightProjection F.obj)) ∧ (∀ F G : Bifibrant S, Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (U.map F G)) ∧ (∀ E : RightFibrations S, ∃ F : Bifibrant S, Enhanced.TransportOverEquivalence E.obj.hom (rightProjection F.obj))
lean.note: The Dwyer--Kan equivalence is rendered by its equivalent explicit clauses: a simplicial map on each actual enriched mapping complex, identity and diagonal-composition preservation, local weak homotopy equivalence and essential surjectivity witnessed by actual over-base inverse homotopies. Its canonical enrichment is normalized on every coherent cone generator by the quotient Q^k to Delta[k], whose composite with the subset-nerve quotient is maximum. All construction helpers belong to this node; no unrelated existence choice or slice-model hypothesis is used.
